bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames McKee’s roughly 62%–38% defeat as a “historic loss,” driven by “backlash” and “traffic chaos” from the Washington Bridge closure, while right-leaning coverage casts Foulkes’s “upset” as “voter anger” over governance and an “avenged” 2022 rematch.
The left stresses McKee’s low approval and the rarity of an incumbent’s collapse; the right emphasizes Democratic vulnerability, Foulkes’s business résumé, and electoral history.

summary: NBC News projected on Thursday that former CVS executive Helena Foulkes defeated incumbent Rhode Island Gov. Dan McKee in the Democratic primary, with public polling showing McKee trailing by double digits heading into Tuesday's vote.

Voter dissatisfaction over the Washington Bridge closure in Providence served as a primary catalyst for the incumbent's defeat; an August Emerson College poll found 63% of likely voters disapproved of McKee's handling of the project.
According to ad-tracking firm AdImpact, Foulkes outspent McKee by a 3-to-1 margin on the airwaves, while emphasizing in campaign ads that the state had "the worst roads and bridges."
Supported by high-profile Democrats including former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi and relatives Thomas Dodd and Chris Dodd, Foulkes is now the heavy favorite in the general election for the blue state.

McKee becomes the first governor to fall in a primary this year, joining a broader anti-incumbent wave that has seen 11 House members lose primaries in 2026, a rarity compared to the 2018 defeat of Kansas Republican Jeff Colyer.
title: Source Icon

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames Fetterman’s Republican-convention video as a “dramatic escalation,” “bombshell,” or even “goes MAGA ,” emphasizing estrangement, “growing rupture,” and party-switch fears; right-leaning accounts portray a “stunning” rebel who is a “common-sense Democrat” resisting the “radical left,” stressing his rejection of “socialism,” support for McCormick, and cooperation with Trump on Pennsylvania steel.
The pivotal divide is whether he merely pledged steel-related cooperation or effectively backed Trump and Republican priorities.

All perspectives stress the appearance’s rarity, cross-party tensions, and steel policy, reflecting broader disputes over Democratic identity, ideological moderation, and Trump-era realignment.
summary: On Wednesday, Democratic Senator John Fetterman will make a surprise video appearance at President Donald Trump 's Republican midterm convention in Dallas, praising the president and discussing the steel industry.
Known as "Trumpapalooza," the event aims to help Republicans maintain their 53-47-seat Senate majority amid vulnerability to Democratic gains in November's midterms.

Fetterman denied plans to leave the Democratic Party, stating, "I'm not going to be a Republican, but I'm going to be a Democrat that's going to have a conversation with whoever is playing it straight."

Recent reports claim he prefers cultivating relationships with conservative commentators over official duties, drawing hostility from Democrats as he has increasingly broken with the party on Israel and Iran policy.
Built on a working-class image that propelled him to victory in 2022, Fetterman has not leveraged his position for party concessions, instead distancing himself from the Democratic Party's left wing.
title: Democratic Sen. John Fetterman to Appear by Video at Trump’s Republican Convention, Reports Say

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames the figures as a “structural shift” and “growing power” for women, spotlighting “stay-at-home men” and women’s majority of workforce jobs as evidence of changing gender roles.

Right-Leaning coverage instead ties nearly all gains to the period “since Trump took office,” using “claimed” and “widened sharply” to emphasize a favorable political-era outcome while highlighting women’s roughly 765,000-job increase against men’s 6,000 decline.
Center coverage foregrounds the 162,000 new jobs, women’s 98% share, and healthcare and education.
All emphasize unusually concentrated gains, but their dividing line is whether the trend signals social transformation, political credit, or economic context.
summary: According to a CNBC analysis of Bureau of Labor Statistics data, women accounted for roughly 98% of August's net payroll gains, capturing 158,000 of the 162,000 jobs added in the month.

Healthcare and local government education sectors fueled this growth, contributing 42,000 jobs in August; women hold nearly three-quarters of positions in these fields, explaining the hiring concentration.
While the female unemployment rate reached 3.9% in August, the male rate rose to 4.4% as the male workforce lost nearly 1.5 million employed workers over the past 12 months.

Laura Ullrich, director of economic research at the Indeed Hiring Lab, cautioned that this concentration may mask negative trends for working mothers, stating, "I don't think it's necessarily a positive story for women overall."

Economists suggest this shift appears more durable than previous instances, as these changes do not resemble recession-driven flips of the past but indicate a long-term structural decline in male labor participation.
title: Women accounted for 98% of the 162,000 US jobs added in August

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames Trump’s forecast that the Iran war will end “immediately” after the midterms as a “wildly” stated, “politically convenient” promise, stressing electoral motives and skepticism about Iran influencing the vote.

All acknowledge the price surge and election-linked timeline, but divide over credibility, Iranian intent, and whether the story is chiefly domestic politics or geopolitical confrontation.
summary: On Wednesday, President Donald Trump predicted the U.S. war with Iran will end "immediately after" the November 3 midterm elections, speaking to reporters before departing Joint Base Andrews for a Republican convention in Dallas.

Renewed hostilities escalated tensions as the U.S. military destroyed 10 Iranian tankers and Iran fired ballistic missiles at American assets, pushing Brent crude above $100 a barrel for the first time since July.
Rising energy costs pushed regular gasoline to $4.22 per gallon, while diesel fuel hit an all-time high of $5.94, according to AAA. Airlines have trimmed schedules and raised fees amid the surge.

Vice-President JD Vance refused to set "artificial timelines" for the conflict's end, contrasting with Trump's post-election prediction. Republicans face pressure defending narrow Congressional majorities as voters express frustration over war and inflation.

Stretching into its seventh month, the conflict defies Trump's initial prediction of a weeks-long engagement. Trump claims Tehran is intentionally prolonging the war to influence the vote, though foreign policy experts argue the administration has run out of options.
title: Trump says oil and gas prices won’t fall until ‘right after’ midterm election

All converge on escalating conflict, Hormuz disruption, falling stocks, and inflation risk, reflecting wider divides over intervention, accountability, and economic consequence.
summary: On Wednesday, Iran attacked over a dozen vessels near the Strait of Hormuz, escalating the six-month conflict after the United States destroyed five Iranian oil tankers on Tuesday and driving Brent prices above $100 per barrel.
Tehran has choked off the strategic Strait while Washington presses a counter-blockade of Iranian ports, creating the largest wave of shipping strikes since the conflict began six months ago.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reported attacking two United States vessels and 10 "non-compliant vessels," while The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said "several" ships in The Gulf were "subject to disabling fire as part of ongoing military activity in the region."

Rising oil prices reflect market fears that the conflict will disrupt supplies, as Iran's foreign ministry labeled the tanker attacks "an overt threat to regional and international peace and security."
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday in Colombia that "Iran continues to try to hit US naval ships," warning the country will lose more tankers in retaliation for each attack.
title: Oil prices rise above $100 a barrel for first time since July as Iran war escalates

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames Trump’s proposed $5,000 payment as a conditional “bribe,” using words like “dangles,” “dubious,” and “Trump-a-Palooza” to stress manipulation, weak polling, empty seats, and a personality-driven party.

Right-Leaning coverage emphasizes “checks for all,” calling it a “dividend,” “populist” incentive, or return from “economic success,” while some skeptics label it an “empty promise” or “Trump show.” Center coverage presents an “extraordinary” financial incentive and foregrounds its estimated $1.35 trillion cost, legal hurdles, and missing funding details.

The pivotal divide is whether the offer represents vote-buying or citizen benefit; all perspectives acknowledge its conditionality, scale, and uncertain implementation, reflecting broader disputes over Trump, government spending, and populist economics.
summary: On Wednesday, President Donald Trump pledged a $5,000 'Trump Dividend' to every U.S. adult if Republicans retain control of both the House and Senate, announcing the proposal at the party's midterm convention in Dallas, Texas.

Seeking to energize voters amid sagging poll numbers, Trump delivered a keynote address at the American Airlines Center, though reporting indicates large sections of the upper level remained empty despite his claims the arena was 'packed.'

Economic analysts estimate the proposal could cost $1.2 trillion, far exceeding roughly $284 billion in tariff revenue collected since January 2025. With national debt exceeding $40 trillion, experts warn the plan lacks funding details and could worsen inflationary pressures.

Critics dismissed the pledge as a campaign stunt, citing legal concerns about linking federal funds to election outcomes. Election law experts noted parallels to billionaire Elon Musk's $1 million payments during the 2025 Wisconsin Supreme Court election.

As the Republican Party grapples with fallout from the unpopular Iran war, Trump vowed to visit battleground states repeatedly to support candidates before the November 3, 2026 elections, attempting to reverse historical midterm losses for the sitting president's party.
title: Trump Promises $5,000 Payment to Every US Adult if GOP Holds Congress

bias: Left-Leaning coverage foregrounds regulatory suspicion, stressing that Nvidia may have “deliberately structured” the Groq licensing deal to “avoid antitrust review,” while highlighting the investigation’s swift timing and formal information request.
Center framing similarly emphasizes “skirt antitrust scrutiny,” but presents the inquiry more institutionally and spotlights the reported $20 billion value.

Right-Leaning coverage adds market consequences, executive moves, Groq’s continued independence, and conflicting $17 billion/$20 billion valuations, framing possible “antitrust evasion” as a risk for investors.
All perspectives agree on DOJ scrutiny and competition concerns, reflecting broader tensions over corporate power, regulation, and market accountability.
summary: On Wednesday, the New York Times reported that the Justice Department is investigating whether Nvidia intentionally structured its licensing deal with AI startup Groq to evade antitrust scrutiny.
Nvidia announced a deal last year for a "non-exclusive license" to Groq's chip technology, hiring founder Jonathan Ross and senior engineers to absorb key talent without an outright acquisition.
Senators Elizabeth Warren and Richard Blumenthal previously questioned the Groq arrangement in March, while Nvidia used a similar $6bn structure with Poolside, hiring 109 staff.
Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo defended the arrangement, stating it is a "prime example of the American system working as designed to promote innovation" and reward entrepreneurs.

Investigators could seek fines if they find wrongdoing, though forcing Nvidia to unwind the deal remains unlikely; the Justice Department sent a formal information request shortly after the deal was announced in December.
title: DOJ probes Nvidia's licensing deal with AI startup Groq, NYT reports

bias: Left-Leaning coverage emphasizes competitive risks, warning Fox might “favor its own content platforms,” while linking scrutiny to Trump’s “blasts” and describing the DOJ’s “closer look” as heightened oversight.

Right-Leaning framing instead foregrounds concentrated corporate power through “Murdoch Empire,” portrays “Washington” as questioning expansion, and uses “deep review” or “offensive” to cast regulation as adversarial; it also highlights Roku’s roughly 2% share decline.
Center coverage stays procedural, stressing a “second request,” a “deeper review,” and possible effects on streaming, advertising, and a 2027 closing.
All perspectives recognize the $22 billion deal and added documents, but diverge over consumer competition versus regulatory overreach and media power.
summary: On Tuesday, the Justice Department widened its antitrust inquiry into Fox's $22 billion acquisition of Roku, planning to issue a 'second request' for additional documents and data from both companies.
Fox unveiled the $160 per share deal months ago, aiming to combine its broadcast and sports operations with Roku's streaming reach to access more than 100 million households using the platform.

With the inquiry in the information-gathering stage, DOJ staff plan to seek more information through a 'second request,' requiring both Fox and Roku to produce substantial additional records in the coming weeks.
Industry rivals have raised concerns that the merged company could favor Fox-owned material, particularly since Roku's free, ad-supported channel already competes for viewers with Fox-owned Tubi.

FOX CEO Lachlan Murdoch previously stated his 'expectation' is to run the two businesses separately while selling advertising across them, and Fox has argued it has a history of growing platforms without shutting out third-party content.
title: US DOJ widens probe into Fox's Roku deal, Semafor reports

Both foreground the Brooklyn trial, alleged trade-secret theft, and the prosecutor’s “criminal enterprise” label, though as an allegation.

summary: On Wednesday, The United States opened a criminal trial against Huawei in Brooklyn federal court, where prosecutors allege two decades of theft, fraud, and racketeering by the world's largest telecom equipment maker.

Prosecutors allege Huawei stole trade secrets from five American companies including Cisco Systems and T-Mobile, citing router source code and a robotic testing device known as Tappy, alongside bank fraud and Iranian sanctions violations.

Defense attorney Brian Heberlig told the jury the case is "about competition, not conspiracy," arguing alleged misconduct involved individual employees rather than a systematic criminal enterprise framing actions as "ordinary business dealings."
The trial is expected to run three months, and a judge ruled that admissions made by former executive Meng Wanzhou remain admissible against Huawei in the proceeding.

While Huawei has been designed out of most Western networks, the proceedings serve as a legal test of past actions, where a conviction could supply a finding of fact tested in open court rather than intelligence assessment.
title: US trial against China's Huawei opens with prosecutor calling the company a criminal enterprise

Right-Leaning coverage acknowledges climate change but qualifies it with El Niño and highlights drought affecting nearly 60% of the country, framing the figures as “worrying” rather than solely ideological proof.
All perspectives agree on NOAA’s record, revealing a broader divide over urgency, causation, and policy implications.
summary: The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration reported Wednesday that the United States experienced its warmest summer in 132 years of recordkeeping, with average temperatures reaching 74.4 degrees Fahrenheit.
This summer's average temperature surpassed previous records set in 1936 and 2021 by 0.4 degrees Fahrenheit, continuing a trend where four of the hottest summers occurred within the past five years.
Nationally, 1,541 record monthly highs were set or tied, while average August temperatures reached 75.6 degrees Fahrenheit—3.5 degrees above the 20th century average.
Powerful heat domes affected nearly every state besides Alaska and Hawaii, driving record-breaking temperatures across the Southwest; Arizona, New Mexico, Utah, and Colorado each set summer records.

Human-Caused climate change alongside a strengthening El Niño pattern is intensifying heat waves and increasing global temperatures, with U.S. summer months warming about 0.46 degrees Fahrenheit per decade since 1970.
title: The U.S. Just Had Its Hottest Summer on Record, NOAA Says

summary: On Wednesday night, President Donald Trump kicked off the inaugural Republican midterm convention in Dallas, urging voters to "pretend that I'm on the ballot" to boost Republican performance in Congress.

Facing record-low approval ratings driven by the Iran war, Trump adopted an unconventional campaign strategy to energize Republican voters and protect congressional majorities during the midterm elections.
Trump proposed a $5,000 dividend to every adult American if Republicans retain both chambers, stipulating that recipients could only spend the money inside the United States.

Dismissing Democratic objections, Trump renewed demands for photo identification and proof of citizenship before voting, then endorsed Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton as a Republican Senate candidate.
Trump suggested the government may need to intervene at Pickaxe Mountain based on reported activity there, a remark that captured his broader unconventional midterm campaign approach.
title: Donald Trump Asks Americans To 'Pretend' He's on Ballot

summary: On Wednesday, Marc Beckman, a senior adviser to Melania Trump , dismissed media speculation regarding Donald Trump's aide Natalie Harp as "absolutely ridiculous," urging journalists to focus on the administration's achievements instead.
Scrutiny intensified this week following reports that Harp, a 35-year-old aide, received a $45,000 gift from Trump, while Melania Trump has appeared in public just about 40 days in 2026.

During an interview posted Wednesday, MAGA host Stella Escobedo accused the media of being "endlessly obsessed with garbage tabloid gossip about Natalie Harp," while Beckman praised Harp as "hardworking."

Beckman asserted the media "doesn't know" about the First Family's private life, arguing journalists should stop focusing on gossip and instead report on the administration's substantial achievements.

While Melania Trump has maintained a relatively low public profile, Beckman pushed back on speculation regarding her absence, claiming reporters ignore the substantial achievements she has conducted during the past year and a half.
title: Melania Trump’s Office Responds to Reports About Donald Trump Aide Natalie Harp

summary: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security announced that tens of thousands of Salvadoran immigrants will maintain their Temporary Protected Status for now, despite protections being scheduled to lapse.

Federal immigration officials stated that an official decision regarding the future of El Salvador's designation will be made at a later date, leaving existing protections and work permits active in the interim.
The temporary extension impacts an estimated 170,000 Salvadorans residing in the United States, a population that advocacy groups estimate contributes $5.4 billion annually to the U.S. economy.
Salvadoran nationals represent one of the largest groups of TPS beneficiaries, having held the humanitarian relief designation continuously following devastating earthquakes in 2001.
The status hold occurs amid broader executive efforts to curtail humanitarian protections and increase restrictions across multiple legal immigration channels.
title: US says immigrants from El Salvador will for now keep temporary protected status

Center coverage de-emphasizes partisan blame, using “conflict” and “may last,” while highlighting shipping attacks and oil above $100.

summary: On Wednesday, Iran attacked 10 ships near the Strait of Hormuz after the USA sank five Iranian oil tankers, marking the largest wave of shipping violence in the six-month-old war.
Benchmark Brent crude futures breached $100 a barrel for the first time since July as shipping flows through the Strait of Hormuz fell to 2 million barrels per day.

At least one seafarer died and another is missing following maritime attacks, while Jordan reported intercepting 18 ballistic missiles fired by Iran at a USA military base with no American casualties.
Top White House advisers, including Vice President Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, warned President Donald Trump the conflict could extend beyond Inauguration Day in January 2029.
President Trump stated on Wednesday he expects the war to end "immediately after" the November midterm elections, arguing Iran is attempting to influence the vote despite cabinet warnings.
title: Trump advisers warn Iran conflict may last through end of his term, WSJ reports

Center coverage presents the renaming as a diplomatic “gesture” and adds conflict chronology, shipping disruption, oil prices, and electoral context.
The pivotal divide is whether the remarks signify vanity or deterrence; all perspectives still emphasize the proposed name, Pickaxe Mountain, “not to get cute,” and escalating U.S.- Iran tensions.
summary: On Wednesday, President Donald Trump warned Iran to be cautious regarding activity at Pickaxe Mountain during a speech at the Republican National Midterm Convention in Dallas, Texas.

Located near Iran's heavily damaged Natanz uranium enrichment facility, the fortified Pickaxe Mountain site hosts two deeply buried tunnel complexes. Trump has threatened strikes on the location since at least mid-July.
Rising oil and gas prices from the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, which began in February, have become a major political issue for Trump and the Republican Party ahead of November midterm elections.
Trump issued a direct warning, stating, "We notice there's a little activity at Pickaxe. I would advise Iran not to get cute because we will have to hit them very hard."
The Republican Party faces mounting pressure to manage the escalating war as officials continue monitoring the fortified site, signaling potential military action if provocations persist.
title: Trump says activity seen at Iran's Pickaxe Mountain, urges Tehran 'not to get cute'

Right-Leaning coverage is briefer, stresses nonprofits “failing to stop” alleged “sexual abuse,” and de-emphasizes “rape,” contextual detail, and defendants.

summary: An 86-year-old woman identified as Jane Doe filed a lawsuit on September 1 in Kern County Superior Court against the Cesar Chavez Foundation and the UFW Foundation, accusing the late civil rights leader Cesar Chavez of raping her in 1973.

The complaint alleges that union leadership maintained a "cult of personality" and hid evidence of misconduct, claiming defendants failed to supervise Chavez or prevent his "abusive, rogue and inappropriate manner" at the La Paz compound.

This lawsuit follows allegations surfaced in March, including claims from UFW co-founder Dolores Huerta, who told the New York Times that Chavez sexually assaulted her in 1966 and pressured her into sexual acts in 1960.

Doe is suing under California Assembly Bill 250, which reopened the statute of limitations for sexual abuse claims. The Cesar Chavez Foundation stated it is reviewing the complaint with legal counsel and will respond accordingly.

A statewide reevaluation of Chavez's legacy followed the accusations, leading officials to rename Cesar Chavez Day to Farmworkers Day and remove the labor leader's name from public schools, streets, and the California Hall of Fame.
title: Former volunteer sues César Chavez nonprofits over failing to stop union leader from sexual abuse

bias: Left-Leaning coverage frames August’s record heat as a climate emergency, stressing “fossil fuels,” the 1.65°C anomaly, the breached 1.5-degree threshold, and “uncharted territory,” with charged phrases such as “Earth cooked” and “sweltered.” Right-leaning coverage accepts warming and El Niño’s contribution but foregrounds “smashes climate records,” “hottest ever,” U.S. heat, and climate-linked landslides and floods, de-emphasizing policy warnings and Western European drought or fires.
Center coverage moderates both with “joint-hottest” and methodological context about the 1940 record and paleoclimate evidence.
All emphasize record heat, ocean warming, and human influence, reflecting a broader divide over urgency, consequences, and fossil-fuel policy.
summary: Earth cooked to its hottest month on record in August, according to European climate service Copernicus, with global temperatures reaching 1.65 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels and exceeding the 1.5 degrees Celsius Paris climate agreement threshold.

While El Niño contributed to the heat, scientists emphasized fossil fuel emissions as the overwhelming driver, with Samantha Burgess, strategic climate lead for Copernicus, noting El Niño adds only one or two tenths of a degree Celsius compared to heat-trapping gases from burning coal, oil and gas.

The Northern Hemisphere experienced its hottest summer on record, with U.S. summer temperatures averaging 23.54 degrees Celsius, while the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration announced summer in the Lower 48 states was hotter than the peak of the devastating Dust Bowl in 1936.

Samantha Burgess warned climate impacts have shifted from abstract concerns to directly disrupting daily lives through school closures, hospital overwhelm and infrastructure failure, stating "the reality is we will get more of these conditions that we've seen this summer."

Climate scientist Zeke Hausfather, Berkeley Earth, projects 2026 will likely beat 2024 as the warmest year on record, with 2027 potentially reaching 1.8 degrees Celsius above preindustrial levels as El Niño strengthens in coming months.
title: August was world's joint-hottest month on record, scientists say

Center-Leaning accounts emphasize a “flip-flop,” balancing the shift with his “safety or fairness” qualification.

summary: On Wednesday, Democratic U.S. Senate nominee James Talarico said he opposes transgender student-athletes competing in girls' sports "if it endangers safety or fairness," reversing his previous legislative record opposing such restrictions in the Texas House.

During the same Fox News interview, Talarico walked back his past claim there are six biological sexes and that "God is non-binary," admitting he had been "provocative" with those statements. He now believes there are two sexes.

Fox News correspondent Brooke Taylor pressed Talarico on his 2021 claim during the interview, while Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton posted on social media calling it a "far-right conspiracy theory." Paxton noted Talarico voted against two bills restricting trans athletes.

Talarico pivoted from the controversy by criticizing Republicans for focusing on his past comments rather than issues like "$6 diesel," while claiming his record looks better compared to his opponent. He accused Paxton of "enriching himself on the public's dime."

This interview occurs as President Donald Trump warns that if Texas turns Blue, he "will be the last Republican president and our country will live in hell," with Talarico attempting the first statewide Democratic win in Texas since 1994.
title: Talarico says he 'missed the mark' in claiming there are 'six sexes'

summary: On Thursday, the Wall Street Journal reported that South Korea is preparing to announce a major energy investment project in the United States worth more than $100 billion aimed at boosting artificial intelligence build-out.

President Donald Trump and President Lee Jae Myung finalized a $350 billion trade deal last October, but implementation delays prompted Trump to threaten tariff hikes on Korean imports previously capped at 15%.

The energy project includes eight nuclear power plants utilizing designs from American firm Westinghouse Electric, while roughly $20 billion is allocated to a Texas natural-gas plant powering AI data centers.
Seoul's trade ministry stated the investment details are not yet finalized, while the White House has not yet responded to the report regarding the financing.
Relations remain strained between the nations, as Washington scaled back military drills last month following Seoul's reported lack of support regarding the conflict involving Iran.
title: South Korea nears agreement worth over $100 billion in US investments, WSJ reports

bias: Left-Leaning coverage mourns a “beloved” and “trusted voice,” emphasizing Melrose’s emotional bond with hockey audiences and the Gretzky-era Kings’ visibility; right-leaning accounts stress his “hard-nosed,” “colorful” persona, defining ESPN legacy, the Kings’ loss in the 1993 Final, and that no official cause of death was released.
Both nevertheless describe his “battle with Parkinson’s,” so that language is shared rather than a partisan dividing line.
Center coverage adds biographical breadth, calling him “legendary” while detailing his playing career.
Across perspectives, reports converge on his death at 70, NHL career, ESPN tenure, and enduring prominence in hockey media.
summary: Barry Melrose, the former NHL player and coach who became a beloved ESPN hockey analyst, died Wednesday at 70. His wife, Cindy, confirmed the death to ESPN's Steve Levy.
Melrose, who served as head coach for the Wayne Gretzky-led Los Angeles Kings, led the team to the Stanley Cup Final in 1993 during his first season. He compiled an 84-108-29 record as a head coach.

His 11-year playing career included over 300 NHL games as a defenseman. He led the Medicine Hat Tigers to a Memorial Cup title in 1987 and guided the Adirondack Red Wings to a 1991 Calder Cup championship.
Renowned for his flashy suits and wit, Melrose frequently covered Stanley Cup playoffs alongside Levy and John Buccigross. Wayne Gretzky called him the "conductor" of the hockey community.
Melrose stepped away from ESPN in 2023 following his Parkinson's disease diagnosis. His legacy spans decades as both a player and broadcaster who remained dedicated to hockey throughout his career.
title: Barry Melrose, former NHL coach and longtime ESPN analyst, dies at 70

summary: On Wednesday, the European Heart Journal published a study linking bedroom light exposure of more than 3 lux to structural changes in the heart, including thickened left-ventricle walls and reduced chamber efficiency.

Analyzing data from more than 11,000 Biobank participants, researchers utilized wrist sensors over seven days to track nighttime light exposure and later assessed heart structure via MRI three years later.

Andrew Freeman, director of cardiovascular prevention and wellness at National Jewish Health in Denver, described the heart muscle thickening as cardiac "remodeling," noting "we don't want the heart muscle to get thick."

Karl Lawrence, a lecturer in the Institute of Pharmaceutical Science at King College London, cautioned that wrist sensors may poorly proxy eye exposure, while other factors like stress account for the remaining 51% of risk.

Experts recommend maintaining bedroom darkness near 1 lux using blackout curtains or sleep masks, as clinicians increasingly consider reducing nighttime light exposure a potential strategy for preventing heart disease.
title: The hidden risk to your heart from sleeping in low light

summary: New York-based Fi recalled two dog supplement products on Tuesday due to potential salmonella contamination, the Food and Drug Administration said.
The company suspended production while investigating an ingredient supplied to its manufacturer, acting "out of an abundance of caution" to address the contamination risk.
Affected products include the 180-gram Calming Supplement, lot 26118, and the 180-gram 8-in-1 Formula Supplement, lot 26159, sold through Amazon and Chewy.
Salmonella infections in pets can cause lethargy, fever, and vomiting, while humans face risks from handling contaminated products or animal waste; no illnesses are currently confirmed.
Owners should immediately discontinue using the supplements, seal containers, and discard them in household trash, or contact Fi daily from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. Eastern time.
title: Supplements for dogs recalled over salmonella risks

title: Multiple US military aircraft suffered damage in overnight strikes on Jordan air base, CBS says

summary: A joint investigation by the New York Times and Flatwater Free Press reported Wednesday that Nebraska Governor Jim Pillen's hog business has employed undocumented workers for over a decade, contradicting his staunch anti- immigration platform.

Pillen, a staunch supporter of President Donald Trump's enforcement policies, has frequently referred to undocumented immigrants as "criminal illegal aliens" who have "invaded our country" while implementing federal immigration partnerships.

The report alleges at least 20 Pillen Family Farms employed undocumented labor, while spokesperson Laura Strimple stated the company "went above and beyond the legal requirements" to verify immigration status and never knowingly hired undocumented workers.

Democratic gubernatorial challenger Lynne Walz and America First Party nominee Brett Lindstrom criticized Pillen Wednesday, arguing the findings show he "plays by his own set of rules" while holding others to different standards.

Shortly after the report's release, Pillen's campaign published "Pillen Playbook 2.0," an updated policy platform outlining new priorities including lower property insurance rates and K-12 funding reform, without addressing the undocumented labor allegations.
title: Nebraska Gov. Pillen Faces Scrutiny Over Family Farm’s Undocumented Workers

summary: Federal and state health officials are investigating a multistate Salmonella outbreak linked to broccoli sprouts from Evergreen Fresh Sprouts LLC, which has sickened 22 people across four states: Washington, Montana, Idaho, and Utah.

Following positive test results in Montana, Evergreen initiated a product recall on September 4, 2026, after state officials identified the outbreak strain in an unopened package collected from a patient's home.
Patient data shows illness onset from July 7 to August 26, 2026, with 89 percent of interviewed individuals specifically recalling eating broccoli sprouts, according to FDA findings.
Consumers should discard or return recalled sprouts with expiration dates of 9/7, 9/9, 9/11, 9/14, and 9/16, and sanitize any surfaces that touched the product.
This outbreak is distinct from separate contamination events involving alfalfa sprouts linked to Everything Fresh Sprouts, as officials continue to monitor for potential new cases.
title: US FDA reports 22 cases of salmonella infections linked to broccoli sprouts

title: Israeli strike kills parents and two children in Gaza, medics say

summary: On Tuesday, Canada joined 11 other nations, including the U.K. and France, in pledging to ban trade in goods from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand said Ottawa will implement restrictions "in the coming months."

The coalition condemned settler violence and settlement expansion, specifically citing the E1 development as actions "tantamount to the annexation of Palestinian land and forcible displacement of the Palestinian population." Twelve nations signed the statement framing these as illegal under international law.

Prime Minister Mark Carney noted the measures build on an advisory issued last month warning businesses of "legal, financial, and reputational risks associated with commercial activities linked to Israeli settlements." The government maintains a two-state solution remains fundamental to peace.

Israeli President Isaac Herzog called the announcement interference in Israel's election, while the foreign minister promised unspecified "counter measures" against participating nations. Israeli ambassador to Canada Iddo Moed warned the move undermines peace prospects and contributes to antisemitism.

Observers noted the ban is likely largely symbolic due to minimal trade volumes between Canada and Israeli settlements. Carney and other leaders plan to co-chair a meeting later this month at the United Nations General Assembly "to advance our efforts and pursue peace.
title: Canada Joins European Ban on Israeli Settlement Goods in Response to Rising Violence

summary: On Tuesday and Wednesday, President Trump's political operation launched Going Back PAC Inc., a new super PAC that began reserving at least $49 million in advertisements to aid Republicans in key battleground races.

Incorporated on Sept 1, Going Back PAC is financially backed by MAGA Inc., President Trump's main super PAC. The spending represents the largest midterm expenditure yet from the $400 million war chest his team promised to deploy.
Data from media tracking firm AdImpact shows the group reserved $9.6 million in New Hampshire on Tuesday, followed by nearly $15 million in Michigan and $11 million in Ohio on Wednesday.

These reservations currently target six Senate races and one House battleground. Due to its Sept 1 incorporation, the organization will not be required to disclose funders or founders until mid-October.

This aggressive spending arrives on the eve of President Trump's unusual two-day convention in Dallas. Meanwhile, Elon Musk's PAC also began spending in more races this week, intensifying the competitive landscape.
title: Trump’s PAC Unloads War Chest, With $47 Million Headed to Key Midterm Races

summary: On Wednesday, host Jimmy Kimmel announced his Thursday interview with Texas Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico will not air on ABC, moving it to YouTube instead due to FCC regulatory concerns.

Kimmel's decision follows ongoing conflict between ABC and the FCC over local station licenses, as ABC sued the agency, alleging the commission is waging an 'extraordinary assault' on its free-speech rights.

In February, CBS lawyers barred Stephen Colbert from airing a Talarico interview citing FCC pressure over equal-time rules; the candidate's campaign raised $2.5 million within 24 hours of the YouTube clip's release.

Kimmel stated, 'Out of consideration for our local stations, especially our ABC affiliates in Texas who would have to deal with this nonsense,' his decision shields the network from potential regulatory backlash.

This situation highlights a broader dispute over political programming and federal equal-time rules for late-night shows; broadcasters navigate heightened FCC scrutiny regarding political candidate appearances even as the agency disputes retaliation allegations.
title: Kimmel Moves Talarico Interview From ABC to YouTube After FCC Threats

summary: On Wednesday, the Justice Department and Education Departments announced findings that Berkeley Law discriminated against white and Asian applicants in its admissions process.

Investigators cited data showing that in 2025, Black applicants had 5.8 times higher odds of admission than comparable white applicants, with significant LSAT score disparities during 2024 and 2025 cycles.

Application questions at Berkeley Law allegedly collected racial information, asking students to specify their identity so admitted individuals could be "grouped" with others of the same "primary identity" in class.
Dean Erwin Chemerinsky denied the allegations, stating the school "will spare no effort to provide ample evidence" that its admissions policies comply with all relevant laws and rules.

Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon alleged the school's efforts "circumvent the Supreme Court 's decision" in SFFA, as the Justice Department seeks a voluntary resolution agreement to ensure legal compliance.
title: Trump administration alleges UC Berkeley School of Law favors Black applicants in admission
